change: Renderer scene admission, bounded text preparation and fallible frame submission
architecture: Validation and resource preparation stay in lucent-render; domain ports, supplied adapters, desktop policy and generated design tokens are unchanged.

admission_limits.geometry: Finite 2^24 coordinate/effect/color envelope; nonnegative dimensions and exact f32 clip indexing
admission_limits.geometry_buffers: Device buffer, clip storage-binding, host slice and draw-index limits; exact-fit fallback when geometric growth exceeds the device limit

rejection_regression: Oversized image, NaN text size and extreme shape geometry fail before resource preparation
A later oversized glyph fails after a valid image upload without changing previous target pixels, geometry-buffer payload or pinned scene resources
A zero-reuse-budget fixture evicts temporary rejected-scene resources while retaining the previous frame
A valid subsequent frame renders on the same canvas and GPU

runtime.notes: Native VM checks. Presentation recovery policy is unit-tested; driver fault injection is not covered here.

native.deployment_scope: Desktop executable only; existing lock/login executables were not replaced

limits: Bounds validate renderer requests; they do not cap total process memory or prove allocation/device-loss recovery
The native runtime still treats a rendering error as fatal; previous-frame retention and subsequent rendering were verified through the offscreen Canvas API
Font parsing and upstream lucent-ui layout admission are separate boundaries
Text rasterization remains synchronous on cache misses; no latency or memory improvement is claimed
Hardware tests are offscreen; native hardware frame pacing, fractional scaling, hotplug and sleep/resume remain unverified
Existing secure lock/unlock passed; interactive root-greeter login was not rerun
